problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface defined in cylindrical polar coordinates as 
$4{r}^{2}-{z}^{2}=0$
for $z\ge 0.$ What is the third component of $f?$
worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of the surface in the form $z=f(r,\theta ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}4{r}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =0 \\ {z}^{2} & =4{r}^{2} \\ z & =\sqrt{4{r}^{2}} \\ z & =2r\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the negative solution since we are given that $z\ge 0.$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(x,y,z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

Now, a point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

$$
f=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩.
$$

Finally, substituting $z=2r,$ we obtain

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,2r⟩.
$$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $2r.$
